title.narrative: Improving Usage of Socio-Economic Statistics for Economic Policy Making in Georgia IDF Grant

description.narrative: The Government is now finalizing its Poverty Reduction and Economic Growth Program (PREGP), which identifies a wide range of strategic goals. The three main building blocks to put in place to achieve a real reduction in poverty as set out in the PREGP are “fast and sustainable economic growth; creation of jobs in the legal sector of the economy; and effective and fair distribution of the resources created in the country.” To be able to monitor and evaluate the progress, the statistical capacities of the government are to be strengthened. At present the instruments and methodologies to produce timely, accurate, and reliable socio-economic data for economic policy design, implementation monitoring, and outcome evaluation are weak, with one of the most uncertain data areas being the national accounts. Undercoverage, underreporting, poor price statistics, etc. affect the quality of GDP estimates, both at current and constant prices, especially at quarterly level and by final consumption categories, thus misleading decision-making in economic policy and evaluation. A long-term methodology for estimating main macro aggregates in a situation of incomplete information should be developed and applied, which would use all available information for checks on completeness and continuity, as well as appropriate methods for scaling/adjustment. Objectives: 1) Increase satisfaction and usage information provided by SDS to targeted institutional agencies (chief among them the Ministry of Finance) by improving SDS understanding of information for results-based public administration, institutional linkages between SDS and other ministries, and users incentives and capacity to use statistical information. 2) Improve SDS efficiency and performance in the compilation of the National Accounts aggregates in two major areas: (i) final consumption estimates, especially those of households; (ii) quarterly GDP estimates at current and constant prices; and in its publicizing/reporting of results through internet tools.
